subject: best practices for a model with two dependent variables

messages.author: 0d4085b4474fa32a
messages.subject: best practices for a model with two dependent variables
parts:
Hi all,

I'm comparing the fit of choice and reaction times with different models (this time everything works!), and I'm making my code nicer and more readable, and adapting it to the latest Stan (to submit it to Stancon :) ). I was wondering if there are best practices for my user-defined probability probability functions. 

Should I add first the choice?

 real race_lpmf(int winner, real rt, row_vector alpha, real sigma){
   ...
 }

or reaction times?

 real race_lpdf(real rt, int winner, row_vector alpha, real sigma){
   ...
 }

And just to be sure, there's no way to move the | after the second argument, right?
In the first case I'll need to do this:

model{
  winner ~ race(rt, alpha, sigma)
}


and it's not possible to do the following, right?

model{
  winner,rt ~ race(alpha, sigma)
}



Bests,
Bruno

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] best practices for a model with two dependent variables
parts:
> On Oct 28, 2016, at 1:06 PM, Bruno Nicenboim <bruno.n...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi all,
>
> I'm comparing the fit of choice and reaction times with different models (this time everything works!), and I'm making my code nicer and more readable, and adapting it to the latest Stan (to submit it to Stancon :) ). I was wondering if there are best practices for my user-defined probability probability functions.
>
> Should I add first the choice?
>
> real race_lpmf(int winner, real rt, row_vector alpha, real sigma){
> ...
> }
>
> or reaction times?
>
> real race_lpdf(real rt, int winner, row_vector alpha, real sigma){
> ...
> }

We don't have conventions for ordering real vs. int arguments
other than that

> And just to be sure, there's no way to move the | after the second argument, right?
> In the first case I'll need to do this:
>
> model{
> winner ~ race(rt, alpha, sigma)
> }
>
>
> and it's not possible to do the following, right?
>
> model{
> winner,rt ~ race(alpha, sigma)
> }

Not yet. In these cases, I'd really recommend just defining
a function race() and using

target += race(winner, rt, alpha, sigma);

because the _lpdf and _lpmf notations are really just for single
outcomes (which can be vectors or matrices, but can't mix integers
and reals yet). It'll be confusing if you have two random
variables (winner and rt) but only one before the ~.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] best practices for a model with two dependent variables
parts:
We probably won't have probability functions with two outcomes,
but we will be adding a tuple type and expressions to build them
that way. But then this mix of real and integer values defeats
our _lpmf vs. _lpdf distinction (which is why I didn't like it in
the first place), as it's neither a pmf nor a pdf. The way it'll
work is:

real foo_lpdf(tuple<matrix,vector> y, matrix theta);

and then you'll be able to write something like

(m, v) ~ foo(theta);

- Bob
